11.web: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your transgressions.”
11.kjv: But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.

11.web: They came again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders came to him,
11.kjv: And they come again to Jerusalem: and as he was walking in the temple, there come to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders,
11.bsb: After their return to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Him.

11.web: and they began saying to him, “By what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”
11.kjv: And say unto him, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority to do these things?
11.bsb: “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You the authority to do them?”

11.web: Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
11.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I will also ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
11.bsb: “I will ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

11.web: The baptism of John—was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”
11.kjv: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? answer me.
11.bsb: John’s baptism—was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!”

11.web: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven;’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
11.kjv: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did ye not believe him?
11.bsb: They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

11.web: If we should say, ‘From men’”—they feared the people, for all held John to really be a prophet.
11.kjv: But if we shall say, Of men; they feared the people: for all men counted John, that he was a prophet indeed.
11.bsb: But if we say, ‘From men’...” they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.

11.web: They answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
11.kjv: And they answered and said unto Jesus, We cannot tell. And Jesus answering saith unto them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
11.bsb: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”

12.web: He began to speak to them in parables. “A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and went into another country.
12.kjv: And he began to speak unto them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it , and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.
12.bsb: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

12.web: When it was time, he sent a servant to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
12.kjv: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.
12.bsb: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

12.web: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.
12.kjv: And they caught him , and beat him, and sent him away empty.
12.bsb: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

12.web: Again, he sent another servant to them; and they threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.
12.kjv: And again he sent unto them another servant; and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.
12.bsb: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.

12.web: Again he sent another; and they killed him; and many others, beating some, and killing some.
12.kjv: And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some.
12.bsb: He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.

12.web: Therefore still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
12.kjv: Having yet therefore one son, his wellbeloved, he sent him also last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.
12.bsb: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

12.web: But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
12.kjv: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.
12.bsb: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

12.web: They took him, killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.
12.kjv: And they took him, and killed him , and cast him out of the vineyard.
12.bsb: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

12.web: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.
12.kjv: What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.
12.bsb: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.

12.web: Haven’t you even read this Scripture: ‘The stone which the builders rejected, the same was made the head of the corner.
12.kjv: And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner:
12.bsb: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

12.web: This was from the Lord, it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
12.kjv: This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?
12.bsb: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

12.web: They tried to seize him, but they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spoke the parable against them. They left him, and went away.
12.kjv: And they sought to lay hold on him, but feared the people: for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way.
12.bsb: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away.

12.web: They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, that they might trap him with words.
12.kjv: And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.
12.bsb: Later, they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words.

12.web: When they had come, they asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and don’t defer to anyone; for you aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?
12.kjv: And when they were come, they say unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Cæsar, or not?
12.bsb: “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one. Indeed, You are impartial and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not? Should we pay them or not?”

12.web: Shall we give, or shall we not give?” But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”
12.kjv: Shall we give, or shall we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said unto them, Why tempt ye me? bring me a penny, that I may see it .
12.bsb: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.”

12.web: They brought it. He said to them, “Whose is this image and inscription?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
12.kjv: And they brought it . And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Cæsar’s.
12.bsb: So they brought it, and He asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.

12.web: Jesus answered them, “Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” They marveled greatly at him.
12.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s, and to God the things that are God’s. And they marvelled at him.
12.bsb: Then Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” And they marveled at Him.

12.web: There came to him Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection. They asked him, saying,
12.kjv: Then come unto him the Sadducees, which say there is no resurrection; and they asked him, saying,
12.bsb: Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him:

12.web: “Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies, and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up offspring for his brother.’
12.kjv: Master, Moses wrote unto us, If a man’s brother die, and leave his wife behind him , and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
12.bsb: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.

12.web: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.
12.kjv: Now there were seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed.
12.bsb: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died, leaving no children.

12.web: The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;
12.kjv: And the second took her, and died, neither left he any seed: and the third likewise.
12.bsb: Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. And the third did likewise.

12.web: and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.
12.kjv: And the seven had her, and left no seed: last of all the woman died also.
12.bsb: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.

12.web: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”
12.kjv: In the resurrection therefore, when they shall rise, whose wife shall she be of them? for the seven had her to wife.
12.bsb: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”

12.web: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God?
12.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?
12.bsb: Jesus said to them, “Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?

12.web: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
12.kjv: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels which are in heaven.
12.bsb: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

12.web: But about the dead, that they are raised; haven’t you read in the book of Moses, about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
12.kjv: And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
12.bsb: But concerning the dead rising, have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses, how God told him, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?

12.web: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”
12.kjv: He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.
12.bsb: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!”

12.web: One of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together. Knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”
12.kjv: And one of the scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, asked him, Which is the first commandment of all?
12.bsb: Now one of the scribes had come up and heard their debate. Noticing how well Jesus had answered them, he asked Him, “Which commandment is the most important of all?”

12.web: Jesus answered, “The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:
12.kjv: And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is , Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord:
12.bsb: Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.

12.web: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
12.kjv: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.
12.bsb: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’

12.web: The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
12.kjv: And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.
12.bsb: The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other commandment is greater than these.”

12.web: The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he,
12.kjv: And the scribe said unto him, Well, Master, thou hast said the truth: for there is one God; and there is none other but he:
12.bsb: “Right, Teacher,” the scribe replied. “You have stated correctly that God is One and there is no other but Him,

12.web: and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
12.kjv: And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.
12.bsb: and to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself, which is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

12.web: When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.” No one dared ask him any question after that.
12.kjv: And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.
12.bsb: When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely, He said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question Him any further.

12.web: Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
12.kjv: And Jesus answered and said, while he taught in the temple, How say the scribes that Christ is the Son of David?
12.bsb: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, He asked, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?

12.web: For David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
12.kjv: For David himself said by the Holy Ghost, The LORD said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool.
12.bsb: Speaking by the Holy Spirit, David himself declared: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

12.web: Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?” The common people heard him gladly.
12.kjv: David therefore himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he then his son? And the common people heard him gladly.
12.bsb: David himself calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?” And the large crowd listened to Him with delight.

12.web: In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,
12.kjv: And he said unto them in his doctrine, Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the marketplaces,
12.bsb: In His teaching Jesus also said, “Watch out for the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, to receive greetings in the marketplaces,

12.web: and the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts:
12.kjv: And the chief seats in the synagogues, and the uppermost rooms at feasts:
12.bsb: and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.

12.web: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
12.kjv: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayers: these shall receive greater damnation.
12.bsb: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”

12.web: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.
12.kjv: And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.
12.bsb: As Jesus was sitting opposite the treasury, He watched the crowd putting money into it. And many rich people put in large amounts.

12.web: A poor widow came, and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.
12.kjv: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.
12.bsb: Then one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which amounted to a small fraction of a denarius.

12.web: He called his disciples to himself, and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,
12.kjv: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:
12.bsb: Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.

12.web: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
12.kjv: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.
12.bsb: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”

13.web: As he went out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”
13.kjv: And as he went out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Master, see what manner of stones and what buildings are here !
13.bsb: As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look at the magnificent stones and buildings!”

13.web: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”
13.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
13.bsb: “Do you see all these great buildings?” Jesus replied. “Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

13.web: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
13.kjv: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,
13.bsb: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked Him privately,

13.web: “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”
13.kjv: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled?
13.bsb: “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to be fulfilled?”

13.web: Jesus, answering, began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
13.kjv: And Jesus answering them began to say, Take heed lest any man deceive you:
13.bsb: Jesus began by telling them, “See to it that no one deceives you.

13.web: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’ and will lead many astray.
13.kjv: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ ; and shall deceive many.
13.bsb: Many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and will deceive many.

13.web: “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
13.kjv: And when ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needs be; but the end shall not be yet.
13.bsb: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.

13.web: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
13.kjv: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows.
13.bsb: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places, as well as famines. These are the beginning of birth pains.

13.web: But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.
13.kjv: But take heed to yourselves: for they shall deliver you up to councils; and in the synagogues ye shall be beaten: and ye shall be brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.
13.bsb: So be on your guard. You will be delivered over to the councils and beaten in the synagogues. On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.

13.web: The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.
13.kjv: And the gospel must first be published among all nations.
13.bsb: And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

13.web: When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand, or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
13.kjv: But when they shall lead you , and deliver you up, take no thought beforehand what ye shall speak, neither do ye premeditate: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye: for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Ghost.
13.bsb: But when they arrest you and hand you over, do not worry beforehand what to say. Instead, speak whatever you are given at that time, for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

13.web: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
13.kjv: Now the brother shall betray the brother to death, and the father the son; and children shall rise up against their parents, and shall cause them to be put to death.
13.bsb: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.

13.web: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
13.kjv: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.
13.bsb: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

13.web: But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,
13.kjv: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand,) then let them that be in Judæa flee to the mountains:
13.bsb: So when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

13.web: and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
13.kjv: And let him that is on the housetop not go down into the house, neither enter therein , to take any thing out of his house:
13.bsb: Let no one on the housetop go back inside to retrieve anything from his house.

13.web: Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
13.kjv: And let him that is in the field not turn back again for to take up his garment.
13.bsb: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.

13.web: But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!
13.kjv: But woe to them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!
13.bsb: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!

13.web: Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.
13.kjv: And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter.
13.bsb: Pray that this will not occur in the winter.

13.web: For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.
13.kjv: For in those days shall be affliction, such as was not from the beginning of the creation which God created unto this time, neither shall be.
13.bsb: For those will be days of tribulation unmatched from the beginning of God’s creation until now, and never to be seen again.

13.web: Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.
13.kjv: And except that the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh should be saved: but for the elect’s sake, whom he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days.
13.bsb: If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.

13.web: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.
13.kjv: And then if any man shall say to you, Lo, here is Christ; or, lo, he is there; believe him not:
13.bsb: At that time if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.

13.web: For there will arise false christs and false prophets, and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
13.kjv: For false Christs and false prophets shall rise, and shall shew signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect.
13.bsb: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform signs and wonders that would deceive even the elect, if that were possible.

13.web: But you watch. “Behold, I have told you all things beforehand.
13.kjv: But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things.
13.bsb: So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance.

13.web: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,
13.kjv: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,
13.bsb: But in those days, after that tribulation: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;

13.web: the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
13.kjv: And the stars of heaven shall fall, and the powers that are in heaven shall be shaken.
13.bsb: the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’

13.web: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
13.kjv: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.
13.bsb: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.

13.web: Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.
13.kjv: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
13.bsb: And He will send out the angels to gather His elect from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven.

13.web: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender, and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;
13.kjv: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When her branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is near:
13.bsb: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.

13.web: even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
13.kjv: So ye in like manner, when ye shall see these things come to pass, know that it is nigh, even at the doors.
13.bsb: So also, when you see these things happening, know that He is near, right at the door.

13.web: Most certainly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
13.kjv: Verily I say unto you, that this generation shall not pass, till all these things be done.
13.bsb: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.

13.web: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
13.kjv: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
13.bsb: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.

13.web: But of that day or that hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
13.kjv: But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.
13.bsb: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

13.web: Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.
13.kjv: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.
13.bsb: Be on your guard and stay alert! For you do not know when the appointed time will come.

13.web: “It is like a man, traveling to another country, having left his house, and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
13.kjv: For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.
13.bsb: It is like a man going on a journey who left his house, put each servant in charge of his own task, and instructed the doorkeeper to keep watch.

13.web: Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming, whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;
13.kjv: Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning:
13.bsb: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know when the master of the house will return—whether in the evening, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.

13.web: lest coming suddenly he might find you sleeping.
13.kjv: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
13.bsb: Otherwise, he may arrive without notice and find you sleeping.

13.web: What I tell you, I tell all: Watch.”
13.kjv: And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.
13.bsb: And what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!”

14.web: It was now two days before the feast of the Passover and the unleavened bread, and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might seize him by deception, and kill him.
14.kjv: After two days was the feast of the passover, and of unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.
14.bsb: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him.

14.web: For they said, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot among the people.”
14.kjv: But they said, Not on the feast day , lest there be an uproar of the people.
14.bsb: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”

14.web: While he was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at the table, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard—very costly. She broke the jar, and poured it over his head.
14.kjv: And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.
14.bsb: While Jesus was in Bethany reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus’ head.

14.web: But there were some who were indignant among themselves, saying, “Why has this ointment been wasted?
14.kjv: And there were some that had indignation within themselves, and said, Why was this waste of the ointment made?
14.bsb: Some of those present, however, expressed their indignation to one another: “Why this waste of perfume?

14.web: For this might have been sold for more than three hundred denarii, and given to the poor.” They grumbled against her.
14.kjv: For it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and have been given to the poor. And they murmured against her.
14.bsb: It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.

14.web: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me.
14.kjv: And Jesus said, Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.
14.bsb: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

14.web: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to, you can do them good; but you will not always have me.
14.kjv: For ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always.
14.bsb: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you will not always have Me.

14.web: She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.
14.kjv: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.
14.bsb: She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.

14.web: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News may be preached throughout the whole world, that which this woman has done will also be spoken of for a memorial of her.”
14.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.
14.bsb: And truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

14.web: Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests, that he might deliver him to them.
14.kjv: And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went unto the chief priests, to betray him unto them.
14.bsb: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.

14.web: They, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. He sought how he might conveniently deliver him.
14.kjv: And when they heard it , they were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.
14.bsb: They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus.

14.web: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare that you may eat the Passover?”
14.kjv: And the first day of unleavened bread, when they killed the passover, his disciples said unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and prepare that thou mayest eat the passover?
14.bsb: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked Him, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”

14.web: He sent two of his disciples, and said to them, “Go into the city, and there you will meet a man carrying a pitcher of water. Follow him,
14.kjv: And he sendeth forth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go ye into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.
14.bsb: So He sent two of His disciples and told them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him,

14.web: and wherever he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
14.kjv: And wheresoever he shall go in, say ye to the goodman of the house, The Master saith, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?
14.bsb: and whichever house he enters, say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’

14.web: He will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”
14.kjv: And he will shew you a large upper room furnished and prepared: there make ready for us.
14.bsb: And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.”

14.web: His disciples went out, and came into the city, and found things as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
14.kjv: And his disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.
14.bsb: So the disciples left and went into the city, where they found everything as Jesus had described. And they prepared the Passover.

14.web: When it was evening he came with the twelve.
14.kjv: And in the evening he cometh with the twelve.
14.bsb: When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.

14.web: As they sat and were eating, Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, one of you will betray me—he who eats with me.”
14.kjv: And as they sat and did eat, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you which eateth with me shall betray me.
14.bsb: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”

14.web: They began to be sorrowful, and to ask him one by one, “Surely not I?” And another said, “Surely not I?”
14.kjv: And they began to be sorrowful, and to say unto him one by one, Is it I? and another said, Is it I?
14.bsb: They began to be grieved and to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?”

14.web: He answered them, “It is one of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.
14.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, It is one of the twelve, that dippeth with me in the dish.
14.bsb: He answered, “It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.

14.web: For the Son of Man goes, even as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
14.kjv: The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had never been born.
14.bsb: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

14.web: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed, he broke it, and gave to them, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body.”
14.kjv: And as they did eat, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and brake it , and gave to them, and said, Take, eat: this is my body.
14.bsb: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take it; this is My body.”

14.web: He took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them. They all drank of it.
14.kjv: And he took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave it to them: and they all drank of it.
14.bsb: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

14.web: He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
14.kjv: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.
14.bsb: He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

14.web: Most certainly I tell you, I will no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”
14.kjv: Verily I say unto you, I will drink no more of the fruit of the vine, until that day that I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
14.bsb: Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”

14.web: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
14.kjv: And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.
14.bsb: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

14.web: Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
14.kjv: And Jesus saith unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.
14.bsb: Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

14.web: However, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
14.kjv: But after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.
14.bsb: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

14.web: But Peter said to him, “Although all will be offended, yet I will not.”
14.kjv: But Peter said unto him, Although all shall be offended, yet will not I.
14.bsb: Peter declared, “Even if all fall away, I never will.”

14.web: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you, that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
14.kjv: And Jesus saith unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this day, even in this night, before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.
14.bsb: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”

14.web: But he spoke all the more, “If I must die with you, I will not deny you.” They all said the same thing.
14.kjv: But he spake the more vehemently, If I should die with thee, I will not deny thee in any wise. Likewise also said they all.
14.bsb: But Peter kept insisting, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the others said the same thing.

14.web: They came to a place which was named Gethsemane. He said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I pray.”
14.kjv: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he saith to his disciples, Sit ye here, while I shall pray.
14.bsb: Then they came to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus told His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”

14.web: He took with him Peter, James, and John, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.
14.kjv: And he taketh with him Peter and James and John, and began to be sore amazed, and to be very heavy;
14.bsb: He took with Him Peter, James, and John, and began to be deeply troubled and distressed.

14.web: He said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch.”
14.kjv: And saith unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death: tarry ye here, and watch.
14.bsb: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”

14.web: He went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
14.kjv: And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
14.bsb: Going a little farther, He fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour would pass from Him.

14.web: He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
14.kjv: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.
14.bsb: “Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.”

14.web: He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour?
14.kjv: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith unto Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldest not thou watch one hour?
14.bsb: Then Jesus returned and found them sleeping. “Simon, are you asleep?” He asked. “Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?

14.web: Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
14.kjv: Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
14.bsb: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”

14.web: Again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.
14.kjv: And again he went away, and prayed, and spake the same words.
14.bsb: Again He went away and prayed, saying the same thing.

14.web: Again he returned, and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy, and they didn’t know what to answer him.
14.kjv: And when he returned, he found them asleep again, (for their eyes were heavy,) neither wist they what to answer him.
14.bsb: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping—for their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to answer Him.

14.web: He came the third time, and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
14.kjv: And he cometh the third time, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough, the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
14.bsb: When Jesus returned the third time, He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? That is enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

14.web: Arise, let us be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”
14.kjv: Rise up, let us go; lo, he that betrayeth me is at hand.
14.bsb: Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!”

14.web: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came—and with him a multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
14.kjv: And immediately, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
14.bsb: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.

14.web: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whomever I will kiss, that is he. Seize him, and lead him away safely.”
14.kjv: And he that betrayed him had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; take him, and lead him away safely.
14.bsb: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.”

14.web: When he had come, immediately he came to him, and said, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.
14.kjv: And as soon as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him.
14.bsb: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Rabbi!” and kissed Him.

14.web: They laid their hands on him, and seized him.
14.kjv: And they laid their hands on him, and took him.
14.bsb: Then the men seized Jesus and arrested Him.

14.web: But a certain one of those who stood by drew his sword, and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
14.kjv: And one of them that stood by drew a sword, and smote a servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
14.bsb: And one of the bystanders drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

14.web: Jesus answered them, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?
14.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Are ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and with staves to take me?
14.bsb: Jesus asked the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?

14.web: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”
14.kjv: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.
14.bsb: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”

14.web: They all left him, and fled.
14.kjv: And they all forsook him, and fled.
14.bsb: Then everyone deserted Him and fled.

14.web: A certain young man followed him, having a linen cloth thrown around himself over his naked body. The young men grabbed him,
14.kjv: And there followed him a certain young man, having a linen cloth cast about his naked body ; and the young men laid hold on him:
14.bsb: One young man who had been following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth around his body. They caught hold of him,

14.web: but he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.
14.kjv: And he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.
14.bsb: but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked.

14.web: They led Jesus away to the high priest. All the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes came together with him.
14.kjv: And they led Jesus away to the high priest: and with him were assembled all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.
14.bsb: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled.

14.web: Peter had followed him from a distance, until he came into the court of the high priest. He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.
14.kjv: And Peter followed him afar off, even into the palace of the high priest: and he sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.
14.bsb: Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.

14.web: Now the chief priests and the whole council sought witnesses against Jesus to put him to death, and found none.
14.kjv: And the chief priests and all the council sought for witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found none.
14.bsb: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.

14.web: For many gave false testimony against him, and their testimony didn’t agree with each other.
14.kjv: For many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together.
14.bsb: For many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent.

14.web: Some stood up, and gave false testimony against him, saying,
14.kjv: And there arose certain, and bare false witness against him, saying,
14.bsb: Then some men stood up and testified falsely against Him:

14.web: “We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.’”
14.kjv: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.
14.bsb: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’”

14.web: Even so, their testimony did not agree.
14.kjv: But neither so did their witness agree together.
14.bsb: But even their testimony was inconsistent.

14.web: The high priest stood up in the middle, and asked Jesus, “Have you no answer? What is it which these testify against you?”
14.kjv: And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?
14.bsb: So the high priest stood up before them and questioned Jesus, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”

14.web: But he stayed quiet, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?”
14.kjv: But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and said unto him, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?
14.bsb: But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”

14.web: Jesus said, “I am. You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of the sky.”
14.kjv: And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
14.bsb: “I am,” said Jesus, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

14.web: The high priest tore his clothes, and said, “What further need have we of witnesses?
14.kjv: Then the high priest rent his clothes, and saith, What need we any further witnesses?
14.bsb: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “Why do we need any more witnesses?

14.web: You have heard the blasphemy! What do you think?” They all condemned him to be worthy of death.
14.kjv: Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.
14.bsb: You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.

14.web: Some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to beat him with fists, and to tell him, “Prophesy!” The officers struck him with the palms of their hands.
14.kjv: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, Prophesy: and the servants did strike him with the palms of their hands.
14.bsb: Then some of them began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers received Him with slaps in His face.

14.web: As Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the maids of the high priest came,
14.kjv: And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:
14.bsb: While Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the servant girls of the high priest came down

14.web: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him, and said, “You were also with the Nazarene, Jesus!”
14.kjv: And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.
14.bsb: and saw him warming himself there. She looked at Peter and said, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”

14.web: But he denied it, saying, “I neither know, nor understand what you are saying.” He went out on the porch, and the rooster crowed.
14.kjv: But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
14.bsb: But he denied it. “I do not know or even understand what you are talking about,” he said. Then he went out to the gateway, and the rooster crowed.

14.web: The maid saw him, and began again to tell those who stood by, “This is one of them.”
14.kjv: And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
14.bsb: There the servant girl saw him and again said to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”

14.web: But he again denied it. After a little while again those who stood by said to Peter, “You truly are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech shows it.”
14.kjv: And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilaean, and thy speech agreeth thereto .
14.bsb: But he denied it again. After a little while, those standing nearby said once more to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean.”

14.web: But he began to curse, and to swear, “I don’t know this man of whom you speak!”
14.kjv: But he began to curse and to swear, saying , I know not this man of whom ye speak.
14.bsb: But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!”

14.web: The rooster crowed the second time. Peter remembered the word, how that Jesus said to him, “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” When he thought about that, he wept.
14.kjv: And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
14.bsb: And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.

15.web: Immediately in the morning the chief priests, with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
15.kjv: And straightway in the morning the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him to Pilate.
15.bsb: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.

15.web: Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answered, “So you say.”
15.kjv: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answering said unto him, Thou sayest it .
15.bsb: So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

15.web: The chief priests accused him of many things.
15.kjv: And the chief priests accused him of many things: but he answered nothing.
15.bsb: And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.

15.web: Pilate again asked him, “Have you no answer? See how many things they testify against you!”
15.kjv: And Pilate asked him again, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they witness against thee.
15.bsb: Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!”

15.web: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate marveled.
15.kjv: But Jesus yet answered nothing; so that Pilate marvelled.
15.bsb: But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply.

15.web: Now at the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whom they asked of him.
15.kjv: Now at that feast he released unto them one prisoner, whomsoever they desired.
15.bsb: Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.

15.web: There was one called Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.
15.kjv: And there was one named Barabbas, which lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.
15.bsb: And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.

15.web: The multitude, crying aloud, began to ask him to do as he always did for them.
15.kjv: And the multitude crying aloud began to desire him to do as he had ever done unto them.
15.bsb: So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.

15.web: Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
15.kjv: But Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
15.bsb: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.

15.web: For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
15.kjv: For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.
15.bsb: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.

15.web: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should release Barabbas to them instead.
15.kjv: But the chief priests moved the people, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.
15.bsb: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.

15.web: Pilate again asked them, “What then should I do to him whom you call the King of the Jews?”
15.kjv: And Pilate answered and said again unto them, What will ye then that I shall do unto him whom ye call the King of the Jews?
15.bsb: So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”

15.web: They cried out again, “Crucify him!”
15.kjv: And they cried out again, Crucify him.
15.bsb: And they shouted back, “Crucify Him!”

15.web: Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, “Crucify him!”
15.kjv: Then Pilate said unto them, Why, what evil hath he done? And they cried out the more exceedingly, Crucify him.
15.bsb: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”

15.web: Pilate, wishing to please the multitude, released Barabbas to them, and handed over Jesus, when he had flogged him, to be crucified.
15.kjv: And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him , to be crucified.
15.bsb: And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.

15.web: The soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and they called together the whole cohort.
15.kjv: And the soldiers led him away into the hall, called Prætorium; and they call together the whole band.
15.bsb: Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.

15.web: They clothed him with purple, and weaving a crown of thorns, they put it on him.
15.kjv: And they clothed him with purple, and platted a crown of thorns, and put it about his head ,
15.bsb: They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.

15.web: They began to salute him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
15.kjv: And began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!
15.bsb: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”

15.web: They struck his head with a reed, and spat on him, and bowing their knees, did homage to him.
15.kjv: And they smote him on the head with a reed, and did spit upon him, and bowing their knees worshipped him.
15.bsb: They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.

15.web: When they had mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put his own garments on him. They led him out to crucify him.
15.kjv: And when they had mocked him, they took off the purple from him, and put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucify him.
15.bsb: After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.

15.web: They compelled one passing by, coming from the country, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them, that he might bear his cross.
15.kjv: And they compel one Simon a Cyrenian, who passed by, coming out of the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to bear his cross.
15.bsb: Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.

15.web: They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, “The place of a skull.”
15.kjv: And they bring him unto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.
15.bsb: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.

15.web: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he didn’t take it.
15.kjv: And they gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.
15.bsb: There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.

15.web: Crucifying him, they parted his garments among them, casting lots on them, what each should take.
15.kjv: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, casting lots upon them, what every man should take.
15.bsb: And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.

15.web: It was the third hour, and they crucified him.
15.kjv: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
15.bsb: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.

15.web: The superscription of his accusation was written over him, “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
15.kjv: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
15.bsb: And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.

15.web: With him they crucified two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.
15.kjv: And with him they crucify two thieves; the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.
15.bsb: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.

15.web: The Scripture was fulfilled, which says, “He was counted with transgressors.”
15.kjv: And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.

15.web: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads, and saying, “Ha! You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days,
15.kjv: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,
15.bsb: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,

15.web: save yourself, and come down from the cross!”
15.kjv: Save thyself, and come down from the cross.
15.bsb: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”

15.web: Likewise, also the chief priests mocking among themselves with the scribes said, “He saved others. He can’t save himself.
15.kjv: Likewise also the chief priests mocking said among themselves with the scribes, He saved others; himself he cannot save.
15.bsb: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!

15.web: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him.” Those who were crucified with him also insulted him.
15.kjv: Let Christ the King of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reviled him.
15.bsb: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.

15.web: When the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
15.kjv: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
15.bsb: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.

15.web: At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interpreted, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
15.kjv: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
15.bsb: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

15.web: Some of those who stood by, when they heard it, said, “Behold, he is calling Elijah.”
15.kjv: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it , said, Behold, he calleth Elias.
15.bsb: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”

15.web: One ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
15.kjv: And one ran and filled a spunge full of vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let alone; let us see whether Elias will come to take him down.
15.bsb: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”

15.web: Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and gave up the spirit.
15.kjv: And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.
15.bsb: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.

15.web: The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
15.kjv: And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.
15.bsb: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

15.web: When the centurion, who stood by opposite him, saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
15.kjv: And when the centurion, which stood over against him, saw that he so cried out, and gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.
15.bsb: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”

15.web: There were also women watching from afar, among whom were both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
15.kjv: There were also women looking on afar off: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
15.bsb: And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

15.web: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and served him; and many other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.
15.kjv: (Who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered unto him;) and many other women which came up with him unto Jerusalem.
15.bsb: These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.

15.web: When evening had now come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
15.kjv: And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,
15.bsb: Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath),

15.web: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for God’s Kingdom, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
15.kjv: Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.
15.bsb: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.

15.web: Pilate marveled if he were already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had been dead long.
15.kjv: And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.
15.bsb: Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.

15.web: When he found out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
15.kjv: And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
15.bsb: When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.

15.web: He bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which had been cut out of a rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
15.kjv: And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.
15.bsb: So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.

15.web: Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, saw where he was laid.
15.kjv: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.
15.bsb: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed.

16.web: When the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, bought spices, that they might come and anoint him.
16.kjv: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.
16.bsb: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus.

16.web: Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
16.kjv: And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun.
16.bsb: Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.

16.web: They were saying among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?”
16.kjv: And they said among themselves, Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre?
16.bsb: They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”

16.web: for it was very big. Looking up, they saw that the stone was rolled back.
16.kjv: And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great.
16.bsb: But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, even though it was extremely large.

16.web: Entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were amazed.
16.kjv: And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were affrighted.
16.bsb: When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.

16.web: He said to them, “Don’t be amazed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been crucified. He has risen. He is not here. Behold, the place where they laid him!
16.kjv: And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.
16.bsb: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.

16.web: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he said to you.’”
16.kjv: But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you.
16.bsb: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”

16.web: They went out, and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had come on them. They said nothing to anyone; for they were afraid.
16.kjv: And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any man ; for they were afraid.
16.bsb: So the women left the tomb and ran away, trembling and bewildered. And in their fear they did not say a word to anyone.

16.web: Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
16.kjv: Now when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.
16.bsb: Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.

16.web: She went and told those who had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
16.kjv: And she went and told them that had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
16.bsb: She went and told those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.

16.web: When they heard that he was alive, and had been seen by her, they disbelieved.
16.kjv: And they, when they had heard that he was alive, and had been seen of her, believed not.
16.bsb: And when they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen Him, they did not believe it.

16.web: After these things he was revealed in another form to two of them, as they walked, on their way into the country.
16.kjv: After that he appeared in another form unto two of them, as they walked, and went into the country.
16.bsb: After this, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.

16.web: They went away and told it to the rest. They didn’t believe them, either.
16.kjv: And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them.
16.bsb: And they went back and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.

16.web: Afterward he was revealed to the eleven themselves as they sat at the table, and he rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they didn’t believe those who had seen him after he had risen.
16.kjv: Afterward he appeared unto the eleven as they sat at meat, and upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not them which had seen him after he was risen.
16.bsb: Later, as they were eating, Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.

16.web: He said to them, “Go into all the world, and preach the Good News to the whole creation.
16.kjv: And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
16.bsb: And He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.

16.web: He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who disbelieves will be condemned.
16.kjv: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
16.bsb: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.

16.web: These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages;
16.kjv: And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues;
16.bsb: And these signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;

16.web: they will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will in no way hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
16.kjv: They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.
16.bsb: they will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.”

16.web: So then the Lord, after he had spoken to them, was received up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of God.
16.kjv: So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God.
16.bsb: After the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, He was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

16.web: They went out, and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word by the signs that followed. Amen.
16.kjv: And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them , and confirming the word with signs following. Amen.
16.bsb: And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked through them, confirming His word by the signs that accompanied it.
